research: Research recommendation separates logical tasks, skill invocations, attempts, and telemetry; aggregates unique eligible task work; treats event count as telemetry.

design.aggregation: Derive orchestrator completion from eligible logical task leaves only: sum(weight * known completion) / sum(weight). Equal weights are the initial fixture. Keep successProgress, failureCount, blockedCount, skippedCount, and eventsObserved separate. If no eligible known nodes exist, aggregate is indeterminate.
design.boundaries: All records are in-memory React state for this educational simulator. No persistence, external side effect, real retry, cancellation guarantee, or server API is introduced.
design.flow: Run start materializes a deterministic task graph and invocation records. Stage transitions update the active task/invocation state and append telemetry. Retry creates an attempt record while preserving logical task/invocation identity. The aggregate selector derives from current task records, never from event count or nested skill bars.
design.identity: Catalog skills remain static by skill.id. Each run creates unique task/invocation/attempt/event IDs. A repeated invocation of the same skill is a distinct invocation record.
design.types: ProgressState = not_started | ready | running | succeeded | failed | blocked | skipped | cancelled | indeterminate. TaskNode has taskId, parentTaskId, label, eligible, weight, state, completion. SkillInvocation has invocationId, taskId, skillId, state, completion. Attempt has attemptId, invocationId, attemptNumber, state, checkpoint. TelemetryEvent has eventId, logicalId, kind, sequence, message. OrchestrationRun has orchestrationId, executionId, taskIds, invocationIds, attemptIds, eventIds.
design.ui: Add an orchestrator summary as the primary surface, task tree/detail as the work breakdown, active skill invocation detail, attempt history, and a separate telemetry count/trace. Keep catalog cards as capability overview with invocation status only; keep the existing five-stage strip as stage progress.
